title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from p.53 and this page. A complex vector space V_C (presumably a (co)homology space with a symplectic form, attached to a curve or covering with dihedral symmetry) splits as V_C = ⊕_{ω∈ω̲} V_C^ω. Since μ_m^{ω̲} has order m², the index set ω̲ has two elements, ω and ω'. Each summand V_C^ω is an isotropic (presumably Lagrangian) subspace, the eigenspace P_ω for the cyclic group D^+ ≅ μ_m (m = 2n), which is the rotation subgroup of a dihedral group D.

How the groups act. μ_m^{ω̲} acts diagonally by componentwise scalars. Scalars μ_m map in diagonally, and D^+ maps by λ ↦ (λ^{a_ω}), with exponents that are presumably ±1, i.e. λ ↦ (λ, λ^{-1}). The resulting map D^+ ×_{μ_m(ω̲)} μ_m → μ_m^{ω̲} has kernel of order 2. Its image has index 2 and is cut out by (λ_ω λ_ω')^n = 1, which is (35).

This page continues as follows.
- The automorphisms of V_C stabilising the distinguished locus V_C^{**} (equivalently, inducing automorphisms of Σ that preserve the extra structure) are those coming from D modulo C^*, i.e. from D × C^*.
- Those that also preserve each P_ω (each isotropic V_C^ω) come from D^+ × C^*.
- Embedding D^+ × C^* into (C^*)^{ω̲} as in (34), the image is the set of (λ_ω, λ_ω') with (λ_ω λ_ω'^{-1})^n = 1, which is (37). Check: (cλ, cλ^{-1}) has ratio λ² ∈ μ_n. The condition does not depend on which ω is singled out.
- For λ_ω, λ_ω' ∈ μ_{2n}, condition (37) is equivalent to the more symmetric form (35), because λ_ω'^{2n} = 1 gives λ_ω'^{-n} = λ_ω'^{n}.
- Hence the elements of μ_{2n}^{ω̲} that violate the relation do not stabilise V^{**}. So the symmetry group is exactly the index-2 subgroup.

Purpose. Grothendieck then states the goal: in each case, choose base points (for the Teichmüller groupoid / fundamental groupoid) stable under D × {1, τ}, where τ is presumably complex conjugation. If possible they should be stable under the larger group ((D × μ_{2n})/{±1}) × {1, τ}, with a remark about the case n = 3 (word read as 'cylindre', uncertain). This prepares the next section on ₀T_{0,5} and S₀T_{0,5}, i.e. the genus-0, 5-point Teichmüller groupoid and its symmetric variant.

The page is a symmetry-group bookkeeping step: compute the stabiliser of a structured eigenspace decomposition, in order to choose maximally symmetric base points.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The equivalence of (37) and (35) holds precisely on μ_{2n}^{ω̲}, as stated; on all of (C^*)^{ω̲} only (37) is the right description.
The exponents a_ω are assumed to be ±1; this is not recoverable from the page alone.

ideas.what: Stabiliser of a pair of complementary isotropic eigenspaces under a dihedral action plus scalars: image of D^+ × C^* in the diagonal torus is {(λ, λ'): (λ/λ')^n = 1}
ideas.modern_name: normaliser / centraliser computation in a maximal torus of GL(V) for a cyclic group action (CM-type eigenspace decomposition)

ideas.what: Choosing base points of Teichmüller groupoids stable under the full symmetry group, including complex conjugation τ
ideas.modern_name: symmetric (tangential) base points; Galois/conjugation-stable base points for profinite Teichmüller groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§ on the Teichmüller tower and choice of base points), in spirit

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computation of a symmetry group in preparation for choosing symmetric base points. The general strategy is already in Esquisse d'un programme, and the page contains no unexpected result.
transcription_corrections: Line 'ce qui, pour λ_ω, λ_ω' ∈ μ_{2n} = μ_m, équivaut à la condition sous la forme (35), plus symétrique' — the transcribed 'μ_{2n}=μ_{2n}[?]' is likely 'μ_{2n} = μ_m'.
'Donc plus symétriques que [?] les éléments...' should probably be split: '(35), plus symétrique. Donc les éléments de μ_{2n}^{ω̲} qui ne satisfont pas cette relation ne stabilisent pas V^{**}'.
'On s'intéresse : des choix de pts pour [?]' should probably read 'On s'intéresse à des choix de pts base qui, dans chaque cas, soient stables par D×{1,τ}'.
In (36) the symbol may be an arrow/embedding D^+×C^* ↪ C^{*ω̲} rather than ⊂.
The final line reading 'cylindre [?] ℤ dans le cas n=3' is uncertain.
